Stara Sil Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Stara Sil, Ukraine

No founding date survives, though the cemetery was marked on an 1880s map; it can be presumed partially demolished after WWII. Jews began settling in Stara Sil in the early 17th century, with a formal community by the 18th, largely employed in salt extraction and trade; a synagogue built in 1765 was ruined during WWII. Population reached 416 (31%) by 1880, declining to 211 by 1921 amid early-20th-century emigration. The Wehrmacht captured the town July 2, 1941; the Jewish population was deported to the Sambir ghetto in March and August 1942.
